questions.title: Which country's mainland coastline will be confirmed contaminated by the Caroline Bezengi oil spill by August 13, 2026?
questions.background: The Caroline Bezengi has been leaking crude oil since running aground in June 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by government environmental authorities, or reliable news reports directly citing those statements. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the country whose mainland coastline is confirmed to have been contaminated by oil from the Caroline Bezengi by August 13, 2026. Offshore pollution, contamination confined to islands, and predictions of future landfall do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Decisive July 24-31 satellite and maritime confirmation (Reuters/Straits Times/gCaptain July 31, The Insider/Greenpeace July 31, Semafor July 28, The Week July 24): after an initial blast off Mukalla, Yemen on June 8, the sanctioned shadow-fleet Suezmax tanker Caroline Bezengi (IMO 9224439) drifted northeast and ran aground on June 12 on rocks off Jazirat Al-Qibliyyah in Oman's Al Hallaniyat Islands — roughly 45 km off Oman's mainland Dhofar/Al Wusta coast and >350 km northeast (downwind/downcurrent) of Yemen. Reuters verified the grounded vessel's identity from deck structures and paint, Greenpeace assessed 3-40 sq km of ongoing crude slicks, and July 28 satellite imagery shows a dark slick near the breached hull with lighter oil patches already spreading north of Al-Qibliyyah directly toward Oman's mainland coastline during peak July-August Southwest Monsoon winds/currents; Oman's Environment Authority issued oil-spill response guidance July 29 after Muscat's July 23 removal ultimatum went unanswered. Moving Oman sharply up (0.42 -> 0.85, capped at 0.85 pending official mainland-contamination confirmation under criteria), slashing Yemen (0.40 -> 0.08, retaining small residual for any delayed claim tied to the June 8 Mukalla blast), and placing small Arabian Sea / Gulf of Oman tails on Pakistan (0.02), Iran (0.02), and India (0.01) (sum 0.98).

questions.title: Which branch of Venezuela's government will the first government–opposition talks after Nicolás Maduro's removal agree to overhaul?
questions.background: Nicolás Maduro was removed from power in January 2026, and Delcy Rodríguez became acting president. Previous negotiations between Venezuela's government and opposition have not produced a lasting political settlement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from the negotiating parties or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera. Resolution Conditions : Identify the branch of government that both sides agree to comprehensively overhaul during their first formal negotiating round following Maduro's January 2026 removal. The round must conclude by August 31, 2026. An announced agreement is sufficient; implementation is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The common name of the governmental branch, rather than an individual institution or officeholder.
questions.current_reasoning: On July 14-15, 2026, National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez and 2015-2020 opposition legislature representative Dinorah Figuera formally announced a US-backed joint work plan starting August 1, 2026 (RNV, Orinoco Tribune, Fakta, ABC Color, The Front Page). Across all coverage and Secretary Marco Rubio's statements, the explicit institutional centerpiece of the August agenda is reforming the electoral system and renewing the National Electoral Council (Electoral branch), even as Trump stated Venezuela is not yet ready for immediate elections and Maria Corina Machado and Edmundo Gonzalez announced on July 26-27 they will not participate. Lifting Electoral branch from 0.58 to 0.64 (below 0.65 before formal agreement) while keeping Judicial branch at 0.22 as the main alternative amid Venezuela's July 24-27 ICC exit and justice disputes.

questions.title: Which Israeli company will Save the Children Norway urge Norway's sovereign wealth fund to divest from by September 20, 2026?
questions.background: Norway's sovereign wealth fund reduced its holdings in Israeli companies in 2025, citing the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the Israeli company publicly identified by Save the Children Norway or its representatives as a divestment target over concerns that its products could contribute to violations of international humanitarian law. Use statements or contemporaneous reporting published between January 1 and September 20, 2026. Answer with the company's full name. Resolution Date : 2026-09-20 Accepted Answer Format : string (company)
questions.current_reasoning: Norway's NBIM reduced its Israeli holdings from 61 to 29 benchmark-listed firms in H2 2025, already divesting Bet Shemesh Engines and excluding five major Israeli banks (Bank Hapoalim, Bank Leumi, Mizrahi Tefahot, FIBI, FIBI Holdings) plus Caterpillar; Elbit Systems was excluded in 2009. Save the Children Norway's divestment target must be a remaining Israeli company whose products raise international humanitarian law concerns, putting defense-tech, chemical, and surveillance suppliers such as Next Vision Stabilized Systems (drone cameras), ICL Group, Cellebrite DI, Aryt Industries, and Gilat Satellite Networks at the top. Because ~29 Israeli holdings remain in NBIM's portfolio plus US-listed Israeli firms, substantial probability mass (0.58) is left unassigned across the wider field.

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Republican U.S. House primary featuring Florida incumbent Cory Mills?
questions.background: Cory Mills is seeking a third term in the U.S. House of Representatives.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Florida Division of Elections results or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations identifying the primary winner. Resolution : Resolve to the winner of the Florida Republican U.S. House primary in which Cory Mills is a candidate, scheduled for August 18, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major tightening ahead of the Aug 18 FL-7 Republican primary (Orlando Sentinel Aug 2, The Floridian July 30, Roll Call July 30, Florida Politics July 20): (1) Incumbent Cory Mills drops 0.60 -> 0.50 after Q2 FEC filings revealed a dramatic fundraising collapse—raising under $60k in Q2 and ending June 30 with just $81,082 cash on hand—amid deepening House Ethics AND Department of Justice investigations, bipartisan resignation calls, an unreachable campaign phone/email, and a 72-20 loss to Elijah in the Seminole County Casselberry straw poll (plus razor-thin 36-35 / 25-20 Volusia chamber tallies). Mills still retains a narrow edge solely because President Trump's endorsement remains intact and the 4-way Florida plurality primary (no runoff) allows Michael Don Johnson (19% in 2024) and Sarah Ulrich to siphon anti-incumbent votes. (2) Former FOX 35 Orlando anchor Ryan Elijah surges 0.32 -> 0.46: he has $268k-$286k cash on hand (>3.3x Mills), launched his first TV ad July 30, consolidated Central Florida GOP leadership (Seminole Sheriff Dennis Lemma, Volusia Sheriff Mike Chitwood, former Rep./AG Bill McCollum, State Sen. Tom Wright, State Rep. Rachel Plakon, Commissioner Amy Lockhart), and positioned himself as pro-Trump while arguing Mills could lose the R+5 seat in November. (3) Michael Don Johnson (0.03 -> 0.02; ballot-removal lawsuit tossed in July, appealing) and Sarah Ulrich (0.05 -> 0.02) both face negligible win odds after openly criticizing Trump and trailing badly in money/endorsements (sum = 1.00 across all 4 certified GOP ballot candidates; sole candidate debate is Aug 5).

questions.title: Who will be appointed to succeed Pape Thiaw as head coach of Senegal's men's national football team by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: The Senegalese Football Federation is responsible for appointing the national team's head coach.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the Senegalese Football Federation, as confirmed by contemporaneous reliable news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the person publicly announced as Pape Thiaw's successor between August 1 and August 31, 2026. The resolution date is the date the appointment is publicly announced, rather than the coach's presentation or first match. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-04 developments: (1) Herve Renard (previously #2 at 0.23) is officially eliminated after Ivory Coast announced his reappointment as head coach today (Reuters/Al Jazeera/Straits Times). (2) Senegalese daily L'Observateur (via Seneweb, Senego, Pulse.sn Aug 4) reveals the FSF is submitting a 3-man shortlist to the Ministry of Sports: Patrick Vieira, Omar Daf, and Herve Renard — leaving Vieira and Omar Daf as the only two surviving shortlistees. (3) Conflicting reports on Patrick Vieira (currently in Senegal since July 29): Afrik-Foot/Sané Malang report Vieira met FSF SG Abdoulaye Sow and reached an agreement held up only by Pape Thiaw's severance indemnity, whereas L'Observateur reports no formal FSF meeting as of Aug 3 midnight, Vieira's preference for a club job, and Ministry of Sports delays demanding World Cup reports before approving Thiaw's exit. Respecting the <=0.55 anti-overconfidence cap on unconfirmed appointments, raise Patrick Vieira 0.42 -> 0.53. Raise Omar Daf sharply 0.12 -> 0.20 as the sole remaining shortlist rival (L'Observateur deems his exit from Congo's assistant role legally possible and credible). Add Souleymane Diallo at 0.08 (explicitly named by Afrik-Foot Aug 4 as FSF's interim backup if Thiaw's severance dispute persists toward September AFCON qualifiers). Hold Habib Beye at 0.07 (free agent since July 1 Marseille exit; top candidate if FSF replaces Renard on the shortlist) and Malick Daf at 0.02 (internal FSF fallback), leaving 10% residual for surprise/replacement candidates.

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 special election for California's 14th congressional district?
questions.background: A special election will fill the U.S. House vacancy created by Eric Swalwell's resignation in April 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Consistent winner projections reported by major U.S. news organizations based on special-election results. Resolution Event : Resolve when a winner is publicly projected for the special election to complete Swalwell's unexpired term. The November 2026 election for the following full term does not count. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: In the June 16, 2026 CA-14 special primary to complete Eric Swalwell's term, State Sen. Aisha Wahab finished first with 42.4%-42.6% (45,380 votes) and BART Board President Melissa Hernandez finished second with 16.7%-16.8% (17,848 votes), advancing to the August 18 special runoff (mirroring their 38.3%-17.2% finish in the June 2 regular primary). Wahab needs less than a fifth of the remaining 40.6% vote pool to cross 50%, and Republican turnout (23.7% in the primary) typically drops in a standalone August Dem-vs-Dem special runoff. Hernandez retains a ~17% upset chance if moderate Democrats, Tri-Valley voters, remaining Republicans, and outside business spending consolidate heavily behind her.

questions.title: Which England bowler will take the most wickets in Pakistan's first innings of the third Test of their 2026 series in England?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the England bowler credited with the most wickets in Pakistan's completed first innings of the third Test of Pakistan's 2026 tour of England. Use the official match scorecard. Resolution Date : 2026-09-09 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the bowler's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Pakistan's third Test in England begins September 9, 2026 (after an eight-day break following the second Test on August 27-31), when cooler autumn conditions typically favor seam bowlers in the first innings. England's June 23 Trent Bridge Test XI confirms Gus Atkinson (7-wicket match-winner at Lord's), Josh Tongue (ever-present vs New Zealand), and Jofra Archer as the frontline pace trio alongside captain Ben Stokes and spinner Shoaib Bashir, while 2024-25 strike seamer Brydon Carse is recovering from a broken wrist and likely available by late August. Accounting for two-and-a-half months of injury, rotation, and single-innings wicket variance, Atkinson (19%), Tongue (15%), Archer (14%), Carse (11%), and Stokes (9%) top the distribution, leaving 32% for Shoaib Bashir, Ollie Robinson, Matthew Fisher, Mark Wood, Matthew Potts, and others.
